subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for Nebula Dynamics - runrate & headroom planning
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@nebuladyn.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@nebuladyn.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for ND app — initial traffic profile

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking this on. High level summary of what we expect from Nebula's production launch (month 1):
- Average request size: ~650 tokens in (prompt + context), responses average ~280 tokens.
- Expected steady-state traffic: 18 req/s, peak burst up to 95 req/s for short windows (10-20m).
- P95 latency target for prompt-to-first-token: <= 180ms.
- Model: we plan to run an open large model variant (medium-large) with KV caching for session continuity.

We need a recommended Dedicated commit (GPU slab + reserve) that meets the SLO and gives sensible headroom for month 1 and month 3 if growth follows the attached conservative/accelerated curves. Please call out: tokens/sec estimates, typical per-vGPU throughput assumptions you used, warm/cold cache impact, autoscale/burst policy, and a short fallback plan if capacity saturates.

I've attached our traffic profiles (nd_commit_runrate.xlsx). Procurement is looped for contract sizing/term questions.

Appreciate an initial sketch by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Best,
Alex
Director of Product, Nebula Dynamics

Attachments: nd_commit_runrate.xlsx (xlsx - traffic profile sheet)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@nebuladyn.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for ND app — initial traffic profile

Alex — thanks for the detailed profile and the spreadsheet. Quick back-of-envelope while we run full sims:

Summary recommendations (top-line):
- Initial Dedicated commit: 6 x vGPU slabs (reserved) + 1 x reserved burst slab (hot pool) as an operable starting point.
- Recommended autoscale policy: immediate burst capacity from hot pool for sustained >60 req/s for >3m, scale-up additional slabs via dedicated autoscale when 95th percentile token/sec consumption > 70% of pooled capacity for 15m.
- Fallback: model variant downgrade (smaller quantized) + aggressive prefix caching for 90s windows, plus queued soft-degrade responses for best-effort throughput preservation.

Key assumptions I used here:
1) Average work per request (roundtrip tokens): 930 tokens total.
2) Effective tokens/sec per vGPU (warm cache, mixed sequence lengths, quantized 4-bit path): ~14,000 tokens/sec. That comes from our internal bench for similar models with sequence mixing and continuous batching.
3) Cold-cache penalty: first request to a session can be 2.5x slower until KV caches warm; assume 10-15% of requests hit cold paths during launches.

Compute math:
- Steady-state tokens/sec = 18 req/s * 930 tokens = 16,740 tokens/sec -> ~1.2 vGPU equivalents (16,740 / 14,000).
- Peak burst tokens/sec = 95 req/s * 930 = 88,350 tokens/sec -> ~6.3 vGPU equivalents.
- Add ~20% headroom for queueing spikes, tail latency, and model variance: peak fit -> 7.6 vGPU -> round up to 8 vGPU-equivalents.

Rounding to Redwood slab sizes (1 slab = 1 vGPU-equivalent for this SKU): propose committing 6 slabs (covering steady-state + expected baseline headroom) and reserving 2 slabs as a burst buffer (1 hot pool + 1 autoscale reserve). That maps to the earlier top-line.

I've kicked off sims with the exact shapes in your spreadsheet; outputs will be in nd_slo_simulation.csv. I attached a quick reasoning note (inline) and will follow up with the simulation CSV and a short runbook for the autoscale policy.

If the procurement team needs a quicker, lower-cost alternative for first 30 days, we can describe a staged commit: 3 slabs committed + 2 slab burst entitlement, then evaluate at day 30 with actual telemetry to finalize.

Logan Wright
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: nd_slo_simulation.csv

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@nebuladyn.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for ND app — initial traffic profile

Alex, Logan — quick add from capacity/ops side with concrete ops controls and SLO mapping.

Operational controls we'd put in the proposal:
- Entitlement map: commit 6 slabs (month 1), with 2 reserved (hot pool + autoscale). Billing model: commit discount applies to the 6 slabs; burst slabs billed at on-demand rate but can be negotiated as partially reserved if you want budget predictability.
- Latency mapping: our tests indicate p95 prompt-to-first-token under 180ms when vGPU utilization < 75% and KV cache hit-rate > 70%. We'll aim to keep the steady-state slab allocation at <= 65% utilization to preserve tail.
- Headroom plan: reserve 20% of aggregate tokens/sec capacity specifically for tail spikes. We'll implement adaptive batching tweaks during peaks (reduce max batch size to favor latency) and enable early-eviction policies on very long sessions.

Deliverables we'll include with the contract:
1) SLA mapping table that ties committed slabs -> expected p50/p95 for both cold and warm cache scenarios.
2) Runbook excerpt for burst events (including who to page, thresholds, and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant).
3) Simulation outputs and the script that produced them (we'll share as zipped artifact).

I'll attach a lightweight diagram of the fallback flow (fallback_flow.png) and the full simulation output (simulation_outputs.zip) to this thread once the runs complete.

Kimberly Park
Principal Capacity Planner — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@nebuladyn.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for ND app — initial traffic profile

Alex — adding a few concrete knobs and a short escalation path.

On Thu, Jun 10, 2027 at 09:15 AM Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the detailed profile and the spreadsheet. Quick back-of-envelope while we run full sims:
> ...

Proposal for knobs: 
- Preemption policy: hot-pool slabs can preempt non-critical background workloads in your environment with 5m advance notice and soft draining; we'll surface a preemption log in the Console.
- Canary window: when adding slabs automatically, we keep an initial 8-minute canary (10% traffic routed) before moving to full scale; this protects against mis-estimating token cost.
- Telemetry hooks: send a daily token-usage digest + p95 latency snapshot to the shared Drive folder; we'll set an automated review if p95 crosses 170ms for 3 consecutive 10-minute windows.

If Nebula prefers lower committed compute to reduce upfront cost, we can present a three-phase commercial with a 30-day evaluation and a mid-term true-up tied to HubSpot deal milestones.

I'll attach a short CSV of the first simulation pass to the HubSpot record and update the DocuSign templates with the slab counts once we agree.

Ben Carter
Deal Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: simulation_outputs.zip
